DATED 28.06.2019 PASSED IN THE CASE NO C.C.NO.14816/2019 DIRECTING THE REGISTRATION OF A CASE AGAINST THE PETITIONER FOR OFFENCE WHICH ARE MADE PENAL U/S.498-A AND 495 OF IPC AND ORDERING PROCESS AGAINST HIM FOR HIS APPEARANCE IN THE CASE BEFORE II ACMM BENGALURU.
(B)QUASH THE PROCEEDINGS THAT ARE BEING RECORDED IN THE CASE.

THIS PETITION, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY,
ORDER WAS MADE THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE M G UMA  ORAL ORDER
Learned counsel for petitioner and respondent No.2 filed the joint memo reporting settlement between the parties.
Petitioner has appeared through video conference and he has been identified by the learned counsel for the petitioner.
Respondent No.2 is present before the Court and identified by the learned counsel for respondent No.2.

The terms of joint memo reads as under:
"1.
It is submitted that the second respondent filed a complaint against the petitioner before first respondent police i.e Chennammanakere Acchukattu Police Station.

The first respondent police registered a case in Crime No. 137/2019 and same is charge sheeted against the petitioner in CC No. 14816/2019 for offences that are made penal under sections 498A, 495 of Indian Penal Code, which is presently pending on the file of XXXVII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Bangalore.

entities.text: XXXVII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court, Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: 2. The second respondent's marriage with the petitioner was solemnized on 16/02/2009 and registered in the office of the Registrar of Marriages, Jayanagar bearing marriage number: JAY- HM720-2008-09 on the same day.

Sri Yathish K vs State Of Karnataka on 9 September, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/188540242/
2

entities.text: Sri Yathish K vs State Of Karnataka
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: 3. The petitioner and the second respondent had earlier obtained a decree of divorce dated 13/02/2014 in M.C. No. 2425/2014 for the marriage that was solemnized on 16/02/2009 which was registered in the office of Registrar of Marriage, Jayanagar on the same day.

4. It is submitted that, with a passage of 2-3 months thereafter, the petitioner and the second respondent as an extension of marriage had ceremonies and got married once again, as per Hindu Rites and Customs, amidst family, friends and relatives on 06/05/2009.

The extension of marriage ceremonies dated 06/05/2009 also came to be registered in the office of the Registrar NC: 2024:KHC:36685 of Marriages,
Jayanagar, Bangalore in JAY-HM106-2015- 16 on 14/05/2015.

5. It is submitted that, the second respondent has filed a petition under section 13(1)(ia) of the Hindu Marriage Act-1955, seeking a decree of divorce in M.C. No.
1856/2023 before the Hon'ble Principal Judge, Family Court, Bengaluru and matter was referred for mediation before the Bangalore Mediation Centre.

In the mediation,
the matter has been settled amicably and the petitioner and the second respondent are entering into Memorandum of Settlement on certain terms and conditions.

6. Further, as per the above mentioned Memorandum of Settlement, one of the conditions is that the 2nd Respondent shall appear before this Hon'ble court in the above case and give her consent for quashing of the proceedings in CC No.
14816/2019 presently pending on the file of the Hon'ble XXXVIIth Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, At Bangalore.

entities.text: XXXVIIth Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, At Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
The petitioner will hand over the DD bearing No.
715011 dated 04/09/2024 drawn on State Bank of India, hanumanthanagar, Branch,
Bangalore for the sum of Rs.15,00,000/- before this Hon'ble Court.
The agreement is attached herewith for the kind perusal of this Hon'ble Court.

7. Since the matter is amicably settled between the parties, the 2nd Respondent herein has no objection to quash the proceedings initiated against the Petitioners in CC No. 14816/2019 presently pending on the file of NC: 2024:KHC:36685 the Hon'ble XXXVIIth Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, At Bangalore.

entities.text: XXXVIIth Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, At Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: In view of the said settlement, this Hon'ble court may be pleased to quash the proceedings in CC No. 14816/2019 presently pending on the file of the Hon'ble XXXVIIth Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, At Bangalore.

entities.text: XXXVIIth Addl. Chief Judicial Magistrate, At Bangalore
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: Hence this Joint Memo."

3. As per the joint memo, the Demand Draft bearing No.715011 dated 04.09.2024 for Rs.15,00,000/- is handed over to respondent No.2.
4.
On enquiry, respondent No.2 submits that she has settled the dispute amicably and she received the Demand Draft for Rs.15,00,000/- towards full and final settlement against the petitioner.
She has no objection to allow the petition.

Accordingly, I proceed to pass the following:
NC: 2024:KHC:36685 ORDER Criminal petition is allowed.

The Criminal proceedings initiated against the petitioner pending in CC No.14816/2019 on the file of the XXXVII Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate Court,
Bangalore for the offence punishable under Sections 498A and 495 of IPC is hereby quashed.
